title: Semantics of copying a register
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers, oracle family $O$, input $x$, and space bound $B$. Let $\mathrm{dst}$ and $\mathrm{src}$ be distinct registers, and suppose the instruction at $\mathrm{test}$ compares them, branching to $\mathrm{ex}$ on equality and to $\mathrm{bump}$ otherwise, while the instruction at $\mathrm{bump}$ increments $\mathrm{dst}$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$. If every current register value is at most $B$ and $v(\mathrm{dst})\le v(\mathrm{src})$, then for any proposition $P$, terminating semantics under the register bound $B$ and acceptance equivalent to $P$ at the configuration with $\mathrm{dst}$ replaced by $v(\mathrm{src})$ imply the same semantics at the original configuration $(\mathrm{test},v,\mathrm{none})$.
